newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES SEND IRABU BACK TO MINORS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES SEND IRABU BACK TO MINORS.

text.p: Four starts after beginning his major-league career with the Yankees, Japanese hurler Hideki Irabu was optioned to New York's Triple-A Columbus team on Monday for some fine tuning.
After an impressive debut on July 10 against Detroit, the right-hander has been hit hard in his last three starts, giving up 17 runs and 20 hits in 13 2/3 innings.
Irabu was rocked on Saturday against Seattle, giving up six runs and four hits -- including two home runs -- in just two innings of work.
Overall this season, Irabu is 2-2 with a 7.97 ERA.
Irabu was acquired by New York from the San Diego Padres in April after lengthy trade talks and signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the World Series champions.

The Yankees shipped $3 million, and a pair of promising players -- outfielder Ruben Rivera and minor league pitcher Rafael Medina -- to San Diego to get Irabu, who was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season with the Chiba Lotte Marines.

The Padres owned Irabu's rights through their working agreement with the Japanese team. Irabu was resolute in his desire to pitch only for the Yankees and said he was prepared to sit out the entire season if he was not traded to New York.
To fill his spot on the roster, the Yankees recalled pitcher Jim Mecir, who was sent down when Irabu was called up from the minors.
